name: should not interleave sequence insertions at the same position
rationale: Concurrent insertion chunks remain contiguous with native and Rust parity.

name: should handle insertion by greater actor ID
rationale: Explicit deterministic actors verify greater-ID insertion ordering.

name: should handle insertion by lesser actor ID
rationale: Explicit deterministic actors verify lesser-ID insertion ordering.

name: should handle insertion after a deleted list element
rationale: Delete/insert concurrency preserves the insertion anchored to a deleted element.

name: rollback_with_no_ops
rationale: Rollback with no pending operations returns zero in native and Rust engines.

name: it should be able to roll back a transaction
rationale: Pending scalar and object operations are rolled back, committed values and heads remain unchanged, and Rust reports the same cancelled operation count.

name: repeated_list_assignment_which_resolves_conflict_not_ignored
rationale: A list element is assigned across a merge and then reassigned; both engines resolve to the single winning value and agree on heads.

name: add_increments_only_to_preceeded_values
rationale: Two actors create and increment separate counters at the same key; the increments stay attached to their own counters, yielding conflicting values 1 and 3 on both engines.

name: assignment_conflicts_of_different_types
rationale: Three actors assign a string, a list, and a map to the same key; both engines pick the same winner and produce identical heads.

name: changes_within_conflicting_map_field
rationale: A string and a populated map conflict at one key; both engines expose the winning map with its inner value and agree on heads.

name: changes_within_conflicting_list_element
rationale: Two actors replace the same list element with maps and mutate them across merges; both engines expose the same winning map contents and heads.

name: concurrently_assigned_nested_maps_should_not_merge
rationale: Two actors assign different maps to the same key; the maps do not merge and the winning map keeps exactly one key on both engines.

name: concurrent_deletion_of_same_list_element
rationale: Both actors delete the same list element concurrently; the element is removed once and the surviving order matches on both engines.

name: concurrent_updates_at_different_levels
rationale: One actor edits a nested map while another deletes it; the deletion wins and only the sibling list remains on both engines.

name: concurrent_updates_of_concurrently_deleted_objects
rationale: One actor updates a nested object another actor deleted concurrently; the deletion wins and the parent becomes empty on both engines.

name: insertion_consistent_with_causality
rationale: Interleaved head insertions across repeated merges produce the causally ordered list one,two,three,four on both engines.

name: save_restore_complex1
rationale: A todo list with a conflicting title survives save and reload; both engines expose both conflicting titles and the retained boolean.

name: save_restore_complex_transactional
rationale: The transactional variant groups writes into single commits; the reloaded document exposes the same conflicting titles and boolean on both engines.

name: big_list
rationale: A list of many null elements is replaced with map objects; both engines materialize N+1 maps that survive a cross-engine save/load with identical heads.

name: invalid_index
rationale: Inserting or putting beyond the end of a list is rejected by both engines while an in-bounds put succeeds.

name: has_our_changes
rationale: Two peers with concurrent changes synchronize until each contains the other's change and both converge to identical heads on both engines.

name: make_sure_load_incremental_doesnt_skip_a_load_with_a_common_head
rationale: Incremental loads that share a common head are not skipped; both engines end with the expected merged two-head frontier.

name: regression_nth_miscount
rationale: A 30-element list of nested maps is indexed after insert-then-replace at every position; both engines resolve each element to the expected map and value with identical heads.

name: regression_nth_miscount_smaller
rationale: A list spanning several op-tree nodes (B*4 elements) is inserted then overwritten at each index; both engines read back every scalar with identical heads.

name: regression_insert_opid
rationale: Interleaved insert-then-overwrite operations round-trip through a cross-engine save/load with every list value preserved and identical heads.

name: rollback_with_several_actors
rationale: Uncommitted edits by a third forked actor are rolled back, leaving the document byte-identical to the forked-from state on both engines.

name: save_with_ops_which_reference_actors_only_via_delete
rationale: A merged delete op references a fork's actor only through successors; the document still saves and reloads cleanly across both engines.

name: simple_bad_saveload
rationale: An empty commit interleaved between real changes does not corrupt the save/load round trip on either engine.

name: bad_change_on_optree_node_boundary
rationale: A document grown across an op-tree node boundary is saved, reloaded elsewhere, and a further change is transferred and reloaded with matching state and heads on both engines.

name: list_counter_del
rationale: Three actors write conflicting counters and an integer to the same list elements; increments apply to every conflicting counter and delete the non-counter, and the conflict sets, lengths, and reloads match the reference engine.

name: first_response_is_some_even_if_no_changes
rationale: Two peers at identical heads still exchange a first sync message so each learns the other's heads.

name: should_allow_simultaneous_messages_during_synchronisation
rationale: Two peers each committing five concurrent changes exchange messages in both directions and converge to identical heads with each other's keys.

name: both_read_only_one_makes_local_changes
rationale: Both peers are read-only; local changes on one are not transferred to the other and the session still quiesces.

name: both_read_only_simultaneous_changes_during_sync
rationale: Both read-only peers make simultaneous changes across two rounds; neither receives the other's data and both quiesce.

name: read_only_peer_new_changes_between_sync_rounds
rationale: A read-only publisher's new changes flow to the read-write peer as a conflict while the publisher never receives the consumer's data.

name: read_only_publisher_to_multiple_consumers
rationale: A read-only publisher's changes reach two independent consumers, and one consumer's changes never reach the other through the publisher.

name: read_only_fully_connected_triangle
rationale: A read-only peer publishes to two read-write peers that then merge; both gain all three change sets while the publisher keeps only its own.

name: stale_shared_heads_after_read_only_sync
rationale: A consumer that already has the read-only publisher's changes via a third peer re-syncs directly and still quiesces without the publisher accepting data.

name: read_only_peer_receives_same_changes_from_two_peers
rationale: A read-only publisher announced the same changes by two peers keeps only its own history and later distributes a new change to both.

name: switch_read_write_to_read_only_mid_session
rationale: A peer switched to read-only mid-session still publishes its own new change but no longer accepts the peer's new change.

name: switch_read_only_to_read_write_with_multiple_rounds
rationale: A read-only peer that ignored several rounds of changes receives all of them after switching to read-write and converges.

name: toggle_read_only_multiple_times
rationale: Toggling read-only on and off across rounds gates change acceptance correctly and converges once read-write.

name: both_toggle_after_multiple_read_only_rounds
rationale: Both peers accumulate changes across read-only rounds and exchange all of them after both switch to read-write.

name: batch_insert_merges_correctly
rationale: Two forks each batch-create a distinct nested map; after merge both objects and their fields are present, verified against the reference.

name: multiple_batch_inserts
rationale: Three sequential batch-created maps each retain their scalar fields on both engines.

name: batch_insert_into_existing_map
rationale: Batch-creating a nested map inside a populated map preserves the existing key and materializes the new nested values.

name: batch_put_overwrite_with_nested_structure
rationale: Overwriting a list element with a deeply nested map and child list keeps the sibling element and materializes the nested structure.

name: splice_merges_correctly
rationale: Concurrent hydrated splices into a shared list merge to length three with the shared element retained.

name: load_incremental_change_without_deps_throws
rationale: Loading a bare change chunk whose dependencies are absent is rejected by both engines.

name: should_not_reply_if_we_have_no_data_after_first_round
rationale: Two empty peers exchange a mandatory first message each, then fall silent once neither has anything to send.

name: read_only_peer_concurrent_changes_during_sync
rationale: A read-only peer that commits a change mid-flight still publishes it to the read-write peer, which the read-only peer never consumes in return.

name: marks_in_spans_cross_block_markers
rationale: A mark spanning text split by a block marker is reported as two marked text spans around the block, identically on both engines.

name: test_mark_behavior_on_delete_insert
rationale: Deleting all marked text and inserting new text leaves the new text unmarked on both engines.

name: spans_consolidates_marks_which_are_empty_due_to_deleted_marks
rationale: Overlapping bold/italic marks partially removed consolidate into the expected three spans on both engines.

name: spans_consolidates_marks_with_deleted_marks_followed_by_empty_marks
rationale: Marking then unmarking a leading range consolidates back to a single unmarked span on both engines.

name: spans_consolidates_marks_with_empty_marks_followed_by_deleted_marks
rationale: Marking then unmarking a trailing range consolidates back to a single span on both engines.

name: text_complex_block_properties
rationale: A block populated with nested text and list properties materializes identical span block values on both engines.

name: mark_created_after_insertion
rationale: Two disjoint strong marks created after insertion produce identical spans on both engines.

name: spans_are_consolidated_in_the_presence_of_zero_length_spans
rationale: Zero-length marks do not fragment the span stream; both engines report a single consolidated text span.

name: empty_marks_before_block_marker_dont_repeat_text
rationale: Empty marks and text inserted around block markers do not duplicate text; both engines report two block spans followed by a single text span.

name: test_splice_with_mark
rationale: Replacing text exactly at two mark boundaries preserves the expanding mark while dropping the non-expanding mark, matching upstream issue #935.

name: get_marks_at_heads
rationale: Marks active at a text index resolved at a historical frontier match the reference after the mark is later removed.

name: inserting_text_near_deleted_marks
rationale: Inserting text around ranges whose marked elements were deleted yields the same active marks as the reference.

name: removed_marks_should_not_appear_in_get_marks
rationale: A mark removed by a null value does not appear in the active mark set on either engine.

name: should_handle_lots_of_branching_and_merging
rationale: Two peers exchange many concurrent changes, a third peer's concurrent change is merged into one, and a final synchronization converges both peers to identical heads on both engines.

name: should support Date objects in maps
rationale: A JavaScript Date stored in a map round-trips through the native Go engine and is re-read identically by JavaScript.

name: should support Date objects in lists
rationale: A JavaScript Date stored in a list round-trips through the native Go engine and is re-read identically by JavaScript.

name: should allow dates from an existing document to be used in another document
rationale: A JavaScript Date read from one document as a timestamp scalar is written into another document through the native engine and re-read as a Date by JavaScript, in both a map and a list.

name: stats_smoke_test
rationale: Two committed puts report two changes, two ops, and one actor identically on the native and reference engines.

name: basic_test
rationale: Materializing a document with a scalar, nested map, list, and text produces the same ordered patch stream on the native and reference engines.

name: test_deleted_ops_omitted
rationale: Deleted scalars, map keys, and list elements are omitted from the materialization patches identically on both engines.

name: test_text_spliced
rationale: Sequential text splices materialize as a single consolidated splice_text patch identically on both engines.

name: test_counters
rationale: A counter with merged increments conflicting with a concurrent value materializes as a conflicted put of the summed counter on both engines.

name: test_multiple_list_insertions
rationale: Multiple list insertions materialize as the same grouped insert patch on both engines.

name: test_concurrent_insertions_at_same_index
rationale: Concurrent insertions at the same index materialize in the same converged order on both engines.

name: test_insert_objects
rationale: Inserting an object into a list materializes the insert and the nested object's properties identically on both engines.

name: test_insert_and_update
rationale: Inserting then overwriting list elements materializes the updated values identically on both engines.

name: diff_should_reverse_deletion_of_object_in_list_correctly
rationale: Diffing after a list-object deletion back to before re-inserts the object and materializes its text identically on both engines.

name: diff_should_reverse_deletion_of_object_in_map_correctly
rationale: Diffing after a map-object deletion back to before re-puts the object and materializes its text identically on both engines.

name: diff_should_reverse_deletion_of_block_in_text_correctly
rationale: Diffing after a text-block deletion back to before re-inserts the block and materializes its properties identically on both engines.

name: large_patches_in_lists_are_correct
rationale: A string list element counts as one index, so a run of 500 following objects is indexed identically in the native and reference diff patch streams.
